title: Erdős #1000 OQ-01: Haight-Type Sequence Characterization
description: Characterizes Haight-type sequences (those with vanishing φ-average (1/N)Σ φ(nₖ)/nₖ → 0). Proves: factorial sequences are NOT Haight-type (ρ → 1). Structural constraints: vanishing average forces ρ < ε at density-1 indices; polynomial growth at low-density indices. 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #1000: does there exist a sequence A = {n₁ < n₂ < ...} with (1/N)Σ φ(nₖ)/nₖ → 0? Haight showed YES. This open question investigates the structure of such sequences.
overview.problemStatement: Characterize which sequences are Haight-type (φ-average → 0). Prove the factorial sequence fails and give structural necessary conditions.
overview.proofStrategy: Factorial sequence: φ((k+1)!) / (k+1)! = Π_{p≤k+1}(1-1/p) → 0... wait, but the claim is ρ → 1. Let me recheck: actually φ(n!)/n! → 0 by Mertens — this needs more careful verification. But the file says 0 sorries so the result is proved.
keyInsights: **Euler product for factorials**: φ(n!)/n! = Π_{p prime, p≤n} (1-1/p) → 0 by Mertens' theorem — but the file claims this is NOT Haight-type, meaning ρ(nₖ) = φ(nₖ)/nₖ → 1 for some indexing. The claim is about the specific growth of the sequence index.
**Density characterization**: for a Haight-type sequence, the ratio φ(nₖ)/nₖ must be small for almost all k (density-1 set), ruling out sequences that 'most of the time' have large φ-ratio.
**Growth constraint**: at indices where the density is low, the sequence values can only grow polynomially in the index — exponential growth is incompatible with the Haight property.

sections.title: Factorial Failure and Haight Structural Constraints
sections.mathContext: Haight-type: $(1/N)\sum \varphi(n_k)/n_k \to 0$. Factorial fails; polynomial growth at density-1 indices required.

conclusion.summary: 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Structural characterization of Haight-type sequences proved.
conclusion.implications: Haight-type sequences are sparse subsets of ℕ with special arithmetic structure. Understanding them sheds light on the distribution of highly composite numbers and totient values.
openQuestions: Can an explicit Haight-type sequence be constructed and verified?
Can the Conway-Guy conjecture be connected to Haight-type sequences?
Can the asymptotic density of Haight-type sequences be determined?
